search_log: Searched: "The Girl Who Kicked the Hornet's Nest" Stieg Larsson excerpt chapter; opened and evaluated the VPM/NPR authorized Chapter 1 excerpt.
Searched: "The Girl Who Kicked the Hornet's Nest" point of view third person narrator; opened the BookRags point-of-view discussion.
Searched publisher, Publishers Weekly, and Google Books combinations; Publishers Weekly results concerned audiobook performance, and no usable Google Books preview was available.

Searched the title with "multiple narrators", epistolary, diary, and "frame narrative"; results did not identify sustained first- or second-person sections, and several uses of 'narrator' referred only to audiobook performers.
Searched the exact title with "third person omniscient" excluding BookRags; opened Patrick Sherriff's review as corroborating whole-book evidence.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person. Numerous interior quote passages externally narrate Salander, Blomkvist, Berger, Faste, and other characters while rendering their private thoughts, matching the authorized opening excerpt and two explicit whole-book POV descriptions. First- and second-person forms in the quotes are dialogue, messages, gnomic statements, or free-indirect wording rather than autonomous base-narrative sections. Historical passages about women warriors are local introductory material rather than a competing narrator. The authorized prose source is limited to the opening, but the varied interior quote evidence and independent whole-book descriptions remove the principal scope uncertainty, and no credible evidence of person alternation was found.
